title: Back then
job: Habits and states in the past; then against now
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: The imperfect L1-M5 opened and L2-M10 used for scenery has a third job, and it is the biggest: HABIT. jugaba is I used to play, not I played once. Nothing in the sentence has to say used to — the tense has already said it.

solía + INFINITIVE is L3-M1's suelo + infinitive moved back one tense. It is not a new verb and not a new pattern: you already own the frame, and this hands you the past of it. Antes solía trabajar los sábados says exactly what trabajaba says, a little more explicitly.

The imperfect has THREE irregular verbs in the entire language — era, iba, veía — and you already have era from L1-M5. Everything else takes -aba or -ía with no surprises, which makes this the cheapest tense in Spanish to learn.

English used to is OPTIONAL: when I was little I ate a lot of bread and I used to eat a lot of bread are the same sentence. So nothing warns you that Spanish has already chosen, and you reach for comí — which says you ate once, on one afternoon, and then stopped.

The then-and-now frame: antes + imperfect against ahora + present, and ya no + present as its negative. L4-M6 opened ya no; here it does the work of a whole second clause — Ya no trabajo allí means the trabajaba is over.

sentences.display: Antes solía trabajar los sábados, ahora no trabajo nunca.
sentences.cue: I used to work Saturdays, now I never work.

words.note: The imperfect of the soler L3-M1 taught as suelo. Same verb, same infinitive after it, one tense further back. It has no other tense worth learning.

sentences.trap: solía trabajar and trabajaba mean the same thing. solía is not stronger or more past — it just says used to out loud, the way English can and Spanish usually does not bother to.
sentences.sound: so-LEE-a. Three syllables: the accent on the i breaks it away from the a that follows.

variations.display: Antes solía trabajar los domingos, ahora no trabajo nunca.
variations.cue: I used to work Sundays, now I never work.
variations.changed: which day the habit sat on

variations.display: Antes solía trabajar mucho, ahora trabajo menos.
variations.cue: I used to work a lot, now I work less.
variations.changed: a change of degree rather than a stop

mistake.display: Antes suelo trabajar los sábados, ahora no trabajo nunca.
mistake.why: suelo is the present, so the sentence says I usually work Saturdays and then denies it in the same breath. antes is not enough to make a present tense past.

sentences.usage: Answering what you used to do for a living, or why your weekends look different. Neutral in both addresses.
sentences.mnemonic: suelo is now, solía is then.

sentences.display: De pequeño jugaba en la calle todos los días.
sentences.cue: As a little boy I played in the street every day.

words.cue: as a child · when I was little
words.note: Two words that behave as one time phrase, and they agree with the speaker: a woman says de pequeña. No verb is needed after it at all.
The imperfect of jugar, and perfectly regular — the u-to-ue change that jugar has in the present does not happen in this tense.

sentences.trap: The English is I played, with no used to in it anywhere. Copy that and you write jugué, which says you played once, on one particular afternoon of your childhood.
sentences.sound: khoo-GA-ba. The j is the throaty one, and the g in the middle is hard.

variations.display: De pequeño jugaba en el parque todos los días.
variations.cue: As a little boy I played in the park every day.

variations.display: De pequeña jugaba en la calle todos los días.
variations.cue: As a little girl I played in the street every day.
variations.changed: the speaker is a woman, so the phrase agrees

mistake.display: De pequeño jugué en la calle todos los días.
mistake.why: jugué is the preterite: one game, one day. With todos los días in the same sentence it collapses — a thing cannot happen once every day.

sentences.usage: Reminiscing with a friend. Intimate, and de pequeño is what people say rather than the fuller cuando era pequeño.
sentences.mnemonic: A childhood is a habit, not an event.

sentences.display: Cuando era pequeño, iba al parque con mi hermana.
sentences.cue: When I was little, I used to go to the park with my sister.

words.note: One of the only three irregular imperfects in Spanish, and it looks nothing like ir. Learn these three and the tense holds no more surprises.

sentences.trap: cuando + imperfect is a scene, not a moment. L4-M6's rule about the subjunctive does not apply here at all: nothing is pending, because this is a childhood that has already been lived.
sentences.sound: EE-ba. Two syllables, and the stress is on the first — not ee-BA.

variations.display: Cuando era pequeño, iba al cine con mi hermana.
variations.cue: When I was little, I used to go to the cinema with my sister.

variations.display: Cuando era pequeño, íbamos al parque los domingos.
variations.cue: When I was little, we used to go to the park on Sundays.
variations.changed: to the whole family, and a day is named

mistake.display: Cuando era pequeño, fui al parque con mi hermana.
mistake.why: fui is one visit. The sentence then reads as a childhood in which the park happened exactly once, which is almost never what is meant.

sentences.usage: Told to somebody who asked where you grew up. Warm, and it works unchanged in usted because no verb in it is addressed to anybody.
sentences.mnemonic: era, iba, veía — the whole irregular list.

sentences.display: En aquella época no había teléfono en casa.
sentences.cue: In those days there was no telephone in the house.

words.note: A stretch of years rather than a clock time, so it never replaces hora or tiempo. L4-M3 taught aquella, and en aquella época is where a Spanish reminiscence usually starts.

sentences.trap: había is L2-M10's and is already an imperfect. It is invariable — there was and there were are both había — so no plural creeps in when the missing thing is plural.
sentences.sound: EH-po-ka. Stress on the first syllable, which the accent marks; the middle o is short.

variations.display: En aquella época no había teléfono en la tienda.
variations.cue: In those days there was no telephone in the shop.

variations.display: En aquella época no había agua en casa.
variations.cue: In those days there was no water in the house.

mistake.display: En aquella época no hubo teléfono en casa.
mistake.why: hubo is the preterite and reports a single event. A decade without a telephone is a state, and states take había.

sentences.usage: Setting a scene for somebody much younger. Neutral, and slightly formal in feel because of aquella.
sentences.mnemonic: A whole era is one long imperfect.

sentences.display: Ya no veo a mis amigos, pero antes los veía mucho.
sentences.cue: I don't see my friends any more, but I used to see them a lot.

words.note: The third and last irregular imperfect. It is irregular only in keeping the e of ver, which the regular pattern would have dropped: not vía but veía.

sentences.trap: ya no takes the PRESENT — ya no veo — even though the change it reports is in the past. The past half of the sentence is carried by veía, not by ya no.
sentences.sound: be-EE-a. Three syllables, and the accent on the i is what keeps them apart.

variations.display: Ya no veo a mis amigos, pero antes los veía todos los días.
variations.cue: I don't see my friends any more, but I used to see them every day.
variations.changed: how often, in the old half

variations.display: Ya no veo a mi hermano, pero antes lo veía mucho.
variations.cue: I don't see my brother any more, but I used to see him a lot.

mistake.display: Ya no veía a mis amigos, pero antes los veía mucho.
mistake.why: Both halves are now in the past, so the then-and-now contrast disappears. ya no is about today and must stay in the present.

sentences.usage: The honest answer to how are things. Neutral, and a common way to say you are lonelier than you were.
sentences.mnemonic: ya no lives in the present; the regret lives in the imperfect.

sentences.display: Antes hacía mucho frío en aquella casa.
sentences.cue: That house used to be very cold.

words.cue: it used to be (of weather) · I / he used to do
words.note: The imperfect of hacer, regular in spite of the verb's reputation. With frío or calor it is the weather verb, and there it has no subject at all.

sentences.trap: Spanish makes cold rather than being cold: hacía frío, never era frío. The house is not the subject — nothing is.
sentences.sound: a-SEE-a. The h is silent, so the word opens on the a and the stress lands on the ee.

variations.display: Antes hacía mucho frío en la cocina.
variations.cue: The kitchen used to be very cold.

variations.display: En aquella época hacía mucho frío en casa.
variations.cue: In those days the house used to be very cold.

mistake.display: Antes era mucho frío en aquella casa.
mistake.why: era translates the English was word for word. Spanish has no was for weather: the verb is hacer, in every tense.

sentences.usage: Complaining fondly about somewhere you used to live. Neutral.

sentences.display: De joven estudiaba por la mañana y trabajaba por la tarde.
sentences.cue: When I was young I studied in the morning and worked in the afternoon.

words.cue: as a young person · in my youth
words.note: Built exactly like de pequeño, and it does not change for a woman because joven has one form for both. It covers roughly the twenties.

sentences.trap: Two habits in one sentence and no y then about it. English would often reach for a used to somewhere; Spanish leaves both verbs bare, because the tense has said it twice already.
sentences.sound: de KHO-ben. The j is throaty and the v is closer to a b.

variations.display: De joven estudiaba por la noche y trabajaba por la mañana.
variations.cue: When I was young I studied at night and worked in the morning.

variations.display: De joven trabajaba mucho y no estudiaba nunca.
variations.cue: When I was young I worked a lot and never studied.
variations.changed: an honest confession replaces the timetable

mistake.display: De joven estudié por la mañana y trabajé por la tarde.
mistake.why: Both preterites turn a couple of years into a single day: one morning of study, one afternoon of work.

sentences.usage: Said across a table to somebody younger, often as the first half of advice. Neutral.
sentences.mnemonic: Two habits, two imperfects, no extra words.

sentences.display: Cuando era pequeña, mi abuela hacía sopa los domingos.
sentences.cue: When I was a little girl, my grandmother used to make soup on Sundays.

words.note: The plural abuelos means grandparents, both of them, the way padres means parents — the masculine plural covers a mixed pair.

sentences.trap: los domingos with the article means on Sundays, every Sunday. Without it, el domingo would be this coming Sunday and the imperfect would have nothing to be habitual about.
sentences.sound: a-BWEH-la. Three syllables, and the ue is one sound.

variations.display: Cuando era pequeña, mi abuela hacía sopa los sábados.
variations.cue: When I was a little girl, my grandmother used to make soup on Saturdays.

variations.display: Cuando era pequeño, mi abuelo hacía sopa los domingos.
variations.cue: When I was a little boy, my grandfather used to make soup on Sundays.

mistake.display: Cuando era pequeña, mi abuela hizo sopa los domingos.
mistake.why: hizo is one pot of soup. Set against los domingos it reads as a single Sunday that somehow repeated, which is why the imperfect exists.

sentences.usage: The most ordinary reminiscence there is. Intimate, and the sort of thing said over a meal.
sentences.mnemonic: los domingos plus the imperfect is every Sunday there ever was.

sentences.cue: Did you use to work there too when you were young?

words.note: The far there, away from both speakers, which is why it pairs so naturally with a past nobody is standing in any more. aquí is its near opposite.

sentences.trap: trabajaba is both I used to work and you (usted) used to work. Usted is written out here for exactly that reason — without it the question could be about the speaker.
sentences.sound: a-YEE. Two syllables, stress on the second, and the double l is a y.

variations.display: ¿Usted también vivía allí de joven?
variations.cue: Did you use to live there too when you were young?

variations.display: ¿Usted también jugaba allí de pequeño?
variations.cue: Did you use to play there too as a child?

mistake.why: trabajó asks about one shift. With de joven attached it becomes a question about a single day in somebody's twenties, which is not what anybody wants to know.

sentences.usage: The same reminiscence as the rest of the module, asked of an older stranger — a neighbour, somebody on a bench. This is the module's one usted item.
sentences.mnemonic: The imperfect does not change for politeness; only the pronoun does.

sentences.display: En aquella época la gente no salía por la noche.
sentences.cue: In those days people didn't go out at night.

words.note: The imperfect of salir, and regular. Note the accent: without it salia would be read with the stress in the wrong place and is not a word.

sentences.trap: la gente is grammatically singular in Spanish — la gente no salía, never no salían. English people is plural and pulls the verb the wrong way.
sentences.sound: sa-LEE-a. Three syllables, and the accent on the i separates it from the a.

variations.display: Antes la gente no salía por la noche.
variations.cue: People didn't used to go out at night.
variations.changed: a plainer way of saying then

variations.display: En aquella época la gente no salía mucho.
variations.cue: In those days people didn't go out much.
variations.changed: the time of day is dropped

mistake.display: En aquella época la gente no salían por la noche.
mistake.why: salían agrees with the English idea of people rather than with the Spanish word. la gente takes a singular verb every time.

sentences.usage: Explaining how a place has changed. Neutral, and often the opening line of a longer story.
sentences.mnemonic: la gente is one crowd, so one verb.

comprehensionPool.display: De pequeño jugaba en el parque.
comprehensionPool.cue: As a little boy I played in the park.

comprehensionPool.display: Cuando era pequeño, iba al cine con mi hermano.
comprehensionPool.cue: When I was little, I used to go to the cinema with my brother.

comprehensionPool.display: En aquella época no había agua caliente.
comprehensionPool.cue: In those days there was no hot water.

comprehensionPool.display: Ya no veo a mis amigos como antes.
comprehensionPool.cue: I don't see my friends the way I used to.

comprehensionPool.display: Antes hacía mucho frío en esta casa.
comprehensionPool.cue: This house used to be very cold.
When I was young I studied and worked.

comprehensionPool.display: Mi abuela hacía sopa todos los días.
comprehensionPool.cue: My grandmother used to make soup every day.
Did you use to live there as a child?

comprehensionPool.display: La gente no salía mucho por la noche.
comprehensionPool.cue: People didn't go out much at night.

comprehensionPool.display: Mis padres solían hablar de aquella época.
comprehensionPool.cue: My parents used to talk about those days.

comprehensionPool.display: Antes vivía aquí, pero ahora vivo lejos.
comprehensionPool.cue: I used to live here, but now I live far away.
